PullRequest.Title: notebook: hide the top insertion toolbar after the first cell is added
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Fixes #350481

The notebook editor announces its model before the top insertion row is attached. The row used to start listening for that announcement only after attachment, so it missed the first model and never noticed the first cell insertion.

Subscribe to model and cell-list changes when the toolbar is constructed. This keeps the row visible while the notebook is empty and restores its existing hover and keyboard-focus behavior as soon as it contains a cell. No CSS or commands change.

### How to test

Create an empty `.ipynb` in Explorer. Click **+ Code** or **+ Markdown**, then move the pointer away with focus in the new cell. The top insertion row should fade without saving or reopening. It should reappear on hover or keyboard focus, and stay visible after deleting the last cell.

### Validation

- `node test\unit\browser\index.js --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\test\browser\cellToolbars.test.ts --browser chromium --reporter spec --stall-timeout 45` — 12 passed. The new test failed before the fix and covers first insertion, last deletion, and model detach.
- `pnpm run oxlint src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\browser\viewParts\notebookTopCellToolbar.ts src\vs\workbench\contrib\notebook\test\browser\cellToolbars.test.ts` — passed.
- A one-off Chromium check exercised both insertion commands, hover, keyboard focus, and last-cell deletion. The patched desktop build was not tested: `pnpm run compile` could not resolve dependencies, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --reporter append-only` returned 404 for the locked `vscode-json-languageservice@6.0.0-next.5`.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an empty or populated notebook and attach its initial view model
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NotebookEditorWidget._attachModel assigns the view model, resolves the output webview, warms up markdown, attaches the list, and fires onDidAttachViewModel. The new model listener performs only updateClass before that existing asynchronous warmup; toolbar construction remains on the attachment event.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Generate webview HTML, create and mount the notebook renderer webview, and wait for initialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One webview initialization per newly attached notebook model; concurrent resolution callers share _webviewResolvePromise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same webview creation and awaited initialization occurred before toolbar attachment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing prerequisite for markdown warmup and list attachment. The changed callback neither invokes nor awaits it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post one initializeMarkup message containing the selected markdown cells and await its acknowledgment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization message per viewport warmup, containing at most five initial markdown cells without cached heights or the selected viewport cells with cached heights. The uncached path can also post a grouped scroll-offset update.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical selection, grouping, serialization, and acknowledgment ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing awaited warmup before list attachment and toolbar creation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One top toolbar per editor widget, one model notification per assignment, and one attachment notification per attachment. Notebook cell count does not increase updateClass cost: getLength reads NotebookViewModel._viewCells.length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The new callback runs synchronously once per model event. Existing webview resolution and markdown initialization are awaited in sequence; the markdown cells are sent as one batch, not one initialization call per cell.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The changed handler has no cache or collection scan. Existing _resolveWebview shares its in-flight promise. With cached cell heights, markdown initialization selects cells intersecting the restored viewport; without them, the initial batch contains at most five markdown cells.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor subscriptions, view-model assignment, constant-time length getter, attachment ordering, and webview messaging were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static review does not measure browser class-mutation or renderer initialization duration; neither operation gains collection-sized work from this diff.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Earlier notification adds a bounded class update on one element without moving heavyweight initialization or boundary calls.

Scenarios.Scenario: Insert, delete, move, or bulk-edit notebook cells, including first insertion and last deletion
Scenarios.CriticalPath: NotebookViewModel updates its cell array and emits one view-cell event containing the computed splices. NotebookEditorWidget forwards that event synchronously; the new listener reads the array length and adds or removes one toolbar class. Existing cell-list rendering proceeds independently of this handler.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send existing markdown-preview creation or update messages to the webview.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A creation message for each eligible markdown cell not already in markupPreviewMapping; existing entries skip recreation and unchanged visible previews skip show updates. Code-only insertion adds no markdown-preview creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same structural-change listener scheduled markdown background rendering and the same preview mapping controlled creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background markdown population is idle-scheduled, not awaited by the new toolbar handler. Existing visible-cell rendering may also request a preview.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One toolbar callback per forwarded structural-change event, not per cell or splice inside that event. Bulk changes with multiple splices produce a single event from compute. Ordinary text edits, scrolling, and output updates do not emit this structural event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changed class callback is synchronous and creates no promises or jobs. Existing background markdown rendering uses a running flag and idle scheduling; preview creation is issued for previously unrepresented, nonhidden markdown cells.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache is needed for the constant-time empty-state query. Existing markdown preview mappings suppress duplicate creation and compare content, metadata, and visibility before posting updates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event payload groups splices, the widget forwards it once, and updateClass does not traverse cells, rebuild menus, or call webview services.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact structural-edit frequency is workload-dependent. Added work is bounded per event, with no demonstrated expensive mechanism or forced layout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly active listener repairs missed empty-state updates; a single class mutation per structural event is not evidence of scaling UI work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change insertion-toolbar settings or edit notebooks with the top toolbar hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing notebook option notifications call updateTopToolbar, replace the current view-zone disposable store, and either reserve whitespace or construct the menu toolbar. Newly permanent model and cell subscriptions only update the existing element's class, including while detached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One subscription pair and one top toolbar element per editor widget. Toolbar rebuilds occur only for relevant option changes or model attachment, not for cell events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous option handling and class updates; no new queue, asynchronous fan-out, or boundary operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: NotebookOptions returns its existing layout configuration. MutableDisposable disposes the previous view-zone store on replacement. No new caches, retained model keys, or menu reconstruction are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both hidden-position early return and visible toolbar construction were inspected. Newly added listeners never call updateTopToolbar or changeViewZones.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Hidden editors now receive a constant-time class update on structural changes, but no expensive work or realistic user-visible degradation is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The earlier subscriptions do not eagerly construct a hidden menu or increase view-zone/layout rebuild frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Detach, replace, reuse, or dispose a notebook editor; hover or keyboard-focus the insertion row
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Detaching clears model-local listeners and assigns an undefined view model, which now updates the toolbar class once. Reattachment uses the existing toolbar rebuild path. Editor disposal explicitly disposes ListTopCellToolbar, whose registered subscriptions are released by Disposable. Hover and focus remain handled by unchanged opacity CSS.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispose the existing notebook output webview and remove its element.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing teardown per model detachment or editor disposal; the new toolbar listener performs no webview teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same model and editor paths disposed the webview before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing synchronous detachment/disposal work, unaffected by the subscription change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two stable editor-owned subscriptions per toolbar across any number of model replacements; no listener accumulation per model or cell. One class operation per model assignment.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous model notifications and disposal. Existing webview teardown remains independent of updateClass; no new scheduled work survives disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new model retention or caches. View-zone replacement continues to dispose old toolbar resources; editor disposal releases the permanent subscription pair.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener ownership was traced through _register, Disposable.dispose, MutableDisposable replacement, and explicit widget disposal. CSS changes only opacity for the empty marker.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Model-switch frequency and browser opacity-transition costs are unmeasured; there is no growing resource count or newly forced layout.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression or high-confidence performance regression fix. The removed missed-event behavior is correctness-related, not evidence of an old expensive mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete two-file inventory and all five hunks. Traced event frequency, constant-time length access, toolbar construction, hidden settings, disposal, and existing batched webview warmup and preview messaging. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression qualifies for reporting. The added test uses bounded mocked resources and suite-owned disposables. Static read-only review; no runtime profiling.
